hypotheses.thesis: A scheduled macro catalyst can release a pre-event volatility compression into a short directional move, but only after price confirms the break and execution costs normalize.
hypotheses.sq_entry_surface: Close breaks the prior volatility-normalized channel after compression; enter next M15 open.
hypotheses.initial_stop: Opposite channel edge or ATR multiple, whichever is tighter within the validated variant.
hypotheses.take_profit: Fixed R multiple selected from a preregistered range.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if OOS expectancy is non-positive under event cost stress or neighboring channel/compression settings are unstable.

hypotheses.thesis: An abnormal short-horizon gold move that fails to hold its extreme can revert part of the displacement when the broader context is range-like rather than a persistent macro repricing.
hypotheses.sq_entry_surface: After an ATR-scaled shock, close re-enters the prior range; enter next M15 open against the failed move.
hypotheses.initial_stop: Beyond the shock extreme plus a small ATR buffer.
hypotheses.take_profit: Prior range midpoint, pre-shock close or fixed R variant.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if trend-regime losses dominate, event-cost stress removes expectancy or stops imply unsafe small-account sizing.

hypotheses.thesis: A compact Asian-session range can expand during the London transition when the break agrees with a pre-existing short trend and monetary-policy regime.
hypotheses.sq_entry_surface: Close breaks the completed Asian range in the aligned direction; enter next M15 open.
hypotheses.initial_stop: Inside/opposite side of the range subject to an ATR safety cap.
hypotheses.take_profit: Range projection or fixed R variant.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if edge is confined to one DST convention/year or conservative costs erase the neighboring parameter region.

hypotheses.thesis: In a range regime, a London break of the Asian range that rapidly closes back inside can revert toward the range midpoint before the session matures.
hypotheses.sq_entry_surface: Price breaks an Asian extreme then closes back inside within a bounded number of M15 bars; enter next open toward the midpoint.
hypotheses.initial_stop: Beyond the failed-break extreme plus ATR buffer.
hypotheses.take_profit: Asian midpoint or opposite quartile, bounded by fixed R.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if reward-to-cost is below the common hurdle or trend-filter neighbors do not separate failures from valid reversions.

hypotheses.thesis: A large equity-index selloff followed by a close-level reclaim can produce a short rebound, provided volatility is no longer accelerating and position risk is scaled down.
hypotheses.sq_entry_surface: After an ATR/percentile selloff, the daily close recovers a preregistered fraction of the range; enter next session open.
hypotheses.initial_stop: Below shock low or ATR multiple with gap stress applied.
hypotheses.take_profit: Short fixed-R rebound or prior close/short moving average.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if crisis folds or gap stress cause unsafe drawdown, or if the VIX/context timestamp is not point-in-time reproducible.

hypotheses.thesis: Short multi-day EURUSD trends can persist after a volatility-normalized breakout when central-bank divergence does not contradict the direction.
hypotheses.sq_entry_surface: Daily close breaks a short prior channel with aligned lagged return; enter next D1 open.
hypotheses.initial_stop: ATR multiple or opposite channel boundary.
hypotheses.take_profit: Fixed R or trailing channel variant.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if performance depends on long historical trends, fails recent regimes or cannot clear rollover and conservative execution costs.
